caption:
Tesla’s new Roadster jumped over five other Tesla vehicles during its October 15 reveal in Texas, using technology developed with SpaceX to launch itself into the air. The car runs on electric motors, but its flying capability comes from a system of high-pressure gas tanks and rocket-style thrusters. These release compressed gas through strategically placed nozzles, generating enough force to lift the car off the ground, control its movement, and bring it back down.

The Roadster also uses four powerful fans underneath its body to create suction, giving the tires enough grip to drive upside down. For airborne maneuvers, additional thrusters point downward and sideways, allowing the car to jump, rotate, and stabilize itself before landing. The most advanced version uses ten thrusters and carries around 250 kilograms of compressed gas. All of this works without traditional rocket fuel or combustion.

There are still some major limitations. The compressed gas runs out quickly, and Tesla has only demonstrated short bursts of flight rather than sustained travel through the air. The full flying system also takes up the passenger seat, turning the Roadster into a single-seater. With production now expected to begin in 2028, Tesla still has to figure out how to turn these impressive demonstrations into something practical. For now, the Roadster offers a pretty wild look at what happens when electric car engineering meets aerospace technology.
